title: India's Defence Stocks Surge as Pinaka Rocket Orders and Record Procurement Drive Rally
excerpt: Solar Industries, BEML, and other defence manufacturers rally to fresh highs as India's defence procurement crosses Rs 6.7 lakh crore in FY26, with the Pinaka rocket system emerging as a major growth catalyst.
body:
• India's Nifty Defence index has hit record highs, with stocks like Solar Industries, BEML, HAL, and Bharat Electronics rallying sharply on the back of Rs 6.7 lakh crore in Defence Acquisition Council procurement clearances during FY26.
  • Solar Industries secured a Rs 6,084 crore Pinaka rocket system contract — the first time a private company has won a contract for India's frontline artillery weapon — pushing its total order book past Rs 17,000 crore.
  • The Ministry of Defence signed Rs 10,147 crore in Pinaka ammunition contracts with Solar's Economic Explosives Limited and state-owned Munitions India Limited in February 2025, covering high-explosive and area denial munitions.
  • Analysts remain bullish on the sector's structural outlook but flag execution risk, with some PSU defence companies facing revenue growth pressure even as private players like Solar Industries post 160% defence revenue growth.

Defence Index Reaches New Highs

India's defence stocks have entered a sustained rally, with the Nifty India Defence index hitting fresh record highs as a combination of massive government procurement, geopolitical tensions, and growing private sector participation drives the sector's rerating.

The broad-based rally has lifted stocks across the spectrum. Solar Industries, which has surged over 330% in two years, trades near Rs 20,000. HAL touched a 52-week high of Rs 5,149.90 on August 17. BEML, Bharat Dynamics, Bharat Electronics, Mishra Dhatu Nigam, and Zen Technologies have all posted sharp gains, with several stocks up 25–80% since Operation Sindoor in May.

The catalyst behind the latest leg higher: the Defence Acquisition Council has cleared procurement proposals worth over Rs 6.7 lakh crore in FY26 alone, covering everything from surface-to-air missiles and loiter munitions to electronic warfare systems and light combat aircraft.

Pinaka Emerges as Growth Engine

Among the specific programmes driving order flows, the Pinaka multiple launch rocket system has emerged as a standout.

Solar Industries secured a Rs 6,084 crore contract in January 2025 for production of Pinaka rockets — marking the first time a private Indian company was awarded a contract for the frontline artillery system. The deal was followed by the Ministry of Defence signing Rs 10,147 crore in Pinaka ammunition contracts in February 2025, split between Solar's subsidiary Economic Explosives Limited and state-owned Munitions India Limited.

The contracts cover two types of munitions: high-explosive pre-fragmented rockets with a 45-kilometre range and area denial munitions effective up to 37 kilometres. The DRDO-developed Pinaka system — capable of launching 12 rockets in 44 seconds — has been deployed along the Line of Actual Control and is being expanded to six additional Army regiments.

"Solar's defence vertical has remained the fastest growing segment in the last five years, with 62% revenue CAGR over FY20-25, led by strong order inflows, healthy execution and a focus on continuously expanding the portfolio."

— Emkay Global Financial Services

In December 2025, the DRDO successfully tested the Pinaka Long Range Guided Rocket with an extended 120-kilometre strike capability, clearing the path for the next generation of orders. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh described the test as a "game changer" for the Armed Forces.

Solar Industries: From Explosives to Aerospace

Solar Industries has transformed from a Nagpur-based commercial explosives manufacturer into one of India's fastest-growing defence companies. Defence revenues surged 160% in FY25, doubling their share of total sales to 18% from 9% the prior year. Management is targeting Rs 3,000 crore in defence revenue for FY26 — implying 120% year-on-year growth — with defence expected to account for 30% of a projected Rs 10,000 crore total revenue.

The company's order book at FY25-end stood at Rs 17,000 crore, more than triple the Rs 5,100 crore recorded in FY24. Beyond Pinaka, Solar is expanding into drones, counter-unmanned aerial systems (the Bhargavastra CUAS), and space propulsion through a partnership with ISRO and an investment in Skyroot Aerospace.

Solar has signed a Rs 12,700 crore memorandum of understanding with the Maharashtra government for a mega defence and aerospace facility in Nagpur, signalling long-term manufacturing ambitions. Its international order book stands at Rs 8,500 crore, with operations across seven countries and new facilities in Saudi Arabia and Kazakhstan under development.

Analysts Flag Execution Divide

While the order pipeline is massive, analysts at ICICI Securities note an emerging divide between private and public sector defence companies. Private players like Solar Industries, PTC Industries, and Astra Microwave Products are expected to sustain healthy earnings growth, with PAT increases of 35–137% year-on-year.

State-run companies face a different picture. HAL's revenue could decline 4% year-on-year in Q4 FY26, while BEL is estimated at just 2% growth, reflecting high base effects and execution headwinds. EBITDA margins at PSUs are expected to contract, with profit after tax declining roughly 10% for both HAL and BEL.

The sector appears to be transitioning into what analysts call a "calibrated phase" of the defence upcycle, where execution efficiency, spending mix, and cash flow delivery matter more than headline order announcements. Key upcoming catalysts include QRSAM missile orders, Nagastra loitering munition deliveries, and the ramp-up in Tejas Mk-1A fighter jet production.
